newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures rise slightly, await NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures rise slightly, await NYMEX.

text.p: IPE oil futures built slightly on Tuesday's upswing but seemed hesitant to break out of a relatively tight range, traders said.
"Everyone is just holding their breath and waiting to see what happens," one trader said.
Dec Brent was trading up 21 cents at $23.59 a barrel at 1240 GMT, while gas oil was up $2.00 at $223.75 a tonne. Both were off their intraday highs.
Dec Brent briefly broke above $23.60 to reach $23.65, but quickly slipped back below the key resistance level, traders said.
They said they did not expect Brent to breach the $23.60 level again on Wednesday, although they said it could be pushed up by NYMEX crude on the weather.
"NYMEX could possibly push it over," the trader said. "It's pretty cold over there."
Frigid temperatures are forecast through the weekend across much of the U.S. as well as parts of Europe, according to Weather Services Corp.
"The weather is really the driving force here," another trader said.
Traders said a cold November would be crucial to keep heating oil stocks from building, and that the market was already looking towards next week's American Petroleum Institute (API) stock figures.
"If November is cold, then you know you won't have a huge stock build," another trader said. "If it doesn't come until January, then forget it. You're too late."

They said gas oil remained clouded by the question of what would happen with the 865,100 tonnes of physical gas oil due to be delivered out of the November IPE gas oil contract. -- Scott McCormack, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8978
